title: Ansible Agentless Automation
summary: A control node reads inventory and playbooks, connects over SSH and runs idempotent modules on managed nodes.

nodes.label: Control Node
nodes.detail: Any machine with Ansible installed. Needs no agent on targets, only SSH access and Python on managed nodes.

nodes.label: Inventory
nodes.detail: Static file or dynamic source listing hosts, groups and variables such as group_vars and host_vars.

nodes.label: Playbook
nodes.detail: YAML mapping host groups to tasks. Plays run top to bottom, with handlers triggered on change.

nodes.label: Roles
nodes.detail: Packaged tasks, templates, defaults and handlers. Roles make automation shareable and testable.

nodes.label: Ansible Vault
nodes.detail: Encrypts sensitive variables so they can be committed to Git and decrypted at run time.

nodes.label: SSH
nodes.detail: Ansible connects with SSH keys, copies a small module payload, runs it and removes it.

nodes.label: Managed Node A
nodes.detail: Target host. Modules compare current and desired state and change only what differs.

nodes.label: Managed Node B
nodes.detail: Another target in a different inventory group, receiving different roles.

nodes.label: Run Result
nodes.detail: The recap shows counts per host. A second run on a converged host reports zero changes.

steps.title: Inventory selects hosts
steps.text: The control node resolves groups and variables from the inventory for the play.

steps.title: Playbook and roles load
steps.text: The playbook lists tasks and roles to apply, with vault-encrypted secrets decrypted in memory.

steps.title: Connect over SSH
steps.text: Ansible opens SSH connections to the managed nodes in parallel.

steps.title: Modules converge state
steps.text: Idempotent modules check current state and change only what differs.

steps.title: Results are reported
steps.text: Each host reports ok, changed or failed, and rerunning should show no changes.
